title: Pennsylvania's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Pennsylvania's 4th Congressional District, covering most of Montgomery County and part of Berks County in the Philadelphia suburbs, is holding a general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democratic U.S. Rep. Madeleine Dean, first elected in 2018, is seeking a fifth term. She faces Republican challenger Aurora Stuski, a small business owner and community activist from West Norriton. The Cook Political Report rates this district as 'Solid Democratic' (D+8 PVI), making Dean the clear favorite in a district that has consistently elected Democrats to Congress since the current district lines were drawn in 2018.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the PA-04 general election were found. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D' and notes the incumbent 'should sail to reelection.' Prediction markets give Democrats a 94% chance of holding the seat.

candidates.name: Madeleine Dean
candidates.summary: Madeleine Dean has served as the U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 4th Congressional District since 2019. She previously served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2018 and was an Abington Township commissioner. Dean serves on the House Appropriations Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and was one of the House impeachment managers for the second impeachment trial of President Donald Trump. Her legislative priorities include public education funding, healthcare access, gun violence prevention, and environmental protection.

candidates.name: Aurora Stuski
candidates.summary: Aurora Stuski is the Republican nominee for Pennsylvania's 4th Congressional District. She is the founder and owner of AAS Appraisal Lab in King of Prussia, a business she has operated since 1989, and holds credentials as a Graduate Gemologist. Stuski has been active in Montgomery County Republican Party politics as Vice Chair of MCRC Area 8 and Chair of the West Norriton Republican Committee. Her campaign focuses on reducing the tax burden on homeowners, protecting seniors on fixed incomes, preserving green space, and supporting community-centered education.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling is available, capping confidence at medium. However, the race data overwhelmingly favor Democratic incumbent Rep. Madeleine Dean: she has won three consecutive terms since the current district lines were drawn in 2018, the district carries a D+8 Cook PVI rating ('Solid Democratic'), prediction markets place Democratic hold probability at 94%, and the challenger (Aurora Stuski, a local GOP activist and small-business owner) faces steep structural odds in a district that has consistently elected Democrats at the federal level. With no polling to refine the margin, the 15-point estimate reflects the district's strong Democratic lean and incumbency advantage.
